task.description: Produce the fix design for ISS-0107 / GitHub #366 per ISSUE-FIXER diagnosis in docs/issues/ISS-0107.json (root_cause, chosen_resolution, files_to_change fields -- read them for full detail). Root cause: tests/integration/helpers.zig TestHarness.init() -- called by every one of the ~19+ test-integration binaries -- runs resetTestData() (TRUNCATE ... RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE on tenant_default.instance_projections, tenant_default.process_definitions, tenant_default.instance_definition_snapshots, tenant_default.tasks) and applyCompatibilityShims() (DROP/CREATE TRIGGER and FUNCTION DDL) completely OUTSIDE the existing bpm_test_migrations_public / per-schema advisory locks, which are released via defer immediately after the migration check-and-apply passes finish earlier in init(). All ~19+ concurrently-running binaries hit this unprotected TRUNCATE/DDL section with zero cross-process ordering, producing N-way circular AccessExclusiveLock waits (genuine Postgres deadlocks, 40P01) plus corroborating trigger-already-exists (42710) and pg_proc unique-violation (23505) errors. This is DDL-vs-DDL (TRUNCATE-vs-TRUNCATE) contention -- every binary is symmetrically both offender and victim, unlike ISS-0106's single-binary ISS-503 case. Chosen resolution: extend the SAME already-correct, already-battle-tested advisory lock in TestHarness.init() to also cover resetTestData()/applyCompatibilityShims(), not just the migration passes -- i.e. widen the locked critical section rather than introducing a new locking mechanism. Single file: tests/integration/helpers.zig only.
acceptance_criteria: Design produces a Type E prose design at src/design/fix-ISS-0107.md

Design addresses the root_cause directly: widen the existing advisory-lock critical section in TestHarness.init() to include resetTestData() and applyCompatibilityShims(), not introduce a new/different locking mechanism or a retry/timeout workaround

Design documents the exact boundary change: where the lock acquire currently happens, where it currently releases (via defer) relative to resetTestData()/applyCompatibilityShims() call sites, and where the lock release must move to so it covers both

Design considers lock contention/performance impact: widening the critical section serializes ALL ~19+ binaries through this section sequentially at startup -- assess whether this is acceptable (it replaces "fails randomly with deadlocks" with "succeeds but with some serialization", which is the same tradeoff WF-03 Step 2 for ISS-0106 already accepted for a similar reason) and state this explicitly as an accepted, understood cost, not an oversight

Design documents whether the lock key/scope used for migrations is appropriate to reuse as-is for resetTestData()/applyCompatibilityShims(), or whether a distinct-but-related key is more correct (e.g. if migrations and reset are conceptually different operations that could theoretically run at different times) -- pick one and justify
No implementation code (no function bodies, no literal diff)
Fix scope <= 5 files, matches files_to_change in ISS-0107.json (tests/integration/helpers.zig)
Error taxonomy section present (state explicitly if none)

Callers/scripts impacted listed (every test-integration binary calls TestHarness.init(), so this is a wide-blast-radius single-file change -- note this explicitly and confirm no binary-specific special-casing is needed since the change is centralized in the shared helper)

result.summary: Produced Type E prose design src/design/fix-ISS-0107.md for ISS-0107 / GitHub #366. The fix widens the existing 'bpm_test_migrations_public' advisory lock already used in TestHarness.init() for the migration passes so it also covers resetTestData() and applyCompatibilityShims(), moving the unlock point from immediately-after-migrations to immediately-after-applyCompatibilityShims(). The design recommends reusing the same lock key (not a distinct one) because the actual invariant needed is mutual exclusion of the whole TestHarness.init() pipeline across processes, not just of the migration phase, and a second key would reopen a cross-key overlap window. It explicitly accepts the added startup serialization across all ~19+ binaries as the same category of tradeoff already accepted in fix-ISS-0106.md, confirms no error-taxonomy changes, and confirms the fix is centralized in tests/integration/helpers.zig only (1 file) with zero binary-specific changes required since every test-integration binary already funnels through the shared TestHarness.init() chokepoint.
